title: Geometry - Lesson 5 Practice: Trapezoids and Kites
description: Practice using trapezoid and kite properties to identify parts and solve measure problems.

questions.question: In a trapezoid, what are the bases?
questions.explanation: The bases of a trapezoid are the parallel sides.

questions.question: A trapezoid has bases 10 cm and 18 cm. What is the length of its median?
questions.explanation: The median is the average of the bases: (10 + 18) / 2 = 14 cm.

questions.question: In an isosceles trapezoid, the diagonals are congruent.
questions.explanation: Congruent diagonals are one of the special properties of an isosceles trapezoid.

questions.question: A kite always has two pairs of opposite congruent sides.
questions.explanation: A kite has two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides, not opposite congruent sides.

questions.question: A trapezoid has median 16 cm and one base 12 cm. If the other base is b, find b.
In a kite, the diagonals are perpendicular. If an angle at their intersection is labeled (5x) degrees, find x.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular diagonals form 90 degree angles. So 5x = 90 and x = 18.

questions.question: Explain why the median of a trapezoid with bases 9 cm and 23 cm is 16 cm.
questions.correctAnswer: The trapezoid median is the average of the two base lengths, so (9 + 23) / 2 = 32 / 2 = 16 cm.
questions.explanation: A correct explanation should identify the bases and use the average formula.

questions.question: A kite has one diagonal that is a line of symmetry. What does that diagonal do to the other diagonal?
questions.correctAnswer: The symmetry diagonal bisects the other diagonal, cutting it into two congruent segments.
questions.explanation: In a kite, the symmetry diagonal bisects the other diagonal. The two split parts of the other diagonal are equal.
